tr: „I don't think that is luck.“
en: „I don't think that is luck.“

tr: Üç özür, tek öğüt. Sorun neymiş?
en: Three apologies, one piece of advice. Where is the problem?

tr: Deneyim sorusu; „before“ en sonda.
en: An experience question; „before“ goes at the end.

tr: „Don't promise. Just write it down.“
en: „Don't promise. Just write it down.“

tr: Bir fotoğraf, bir aile. Kim kimin nesi?
en: One photo, one family. Who is who?

tr: Bir fotoğraf dolaşıyor. Ne kadarı doğru?
en: A photo is going around. How much of it is true?

tr: „…the answer is two words: You're welcome.“
en: „…the answer is two words: You're welcome.“

tr: „Done. Tuesday, ten o'clock, with a sound.“
en: „Done. Tuesday, ten o'clock, with a sound.“

tr: Deneyim sorusu: „see“nin üçüncü hâli „seen“.
en: An experience question: the third form of „see“ is „seen“.

tr: Yeni bir dizi. Kaç bölüm izlendi, konusu ne?
en: A new series. How many episodes are watched, and what is it about?

tr: „But I don't believe you can stop it either.“
en: „But I don't believe you can stop it either.“

tr: „I'm not ready. Three chapters and two days.“
en: „I'm not ready. Three chapters and two days.“

tr: „It's a tradition to“ sonrası mastar geliyor.
en: After „It's a tradition to“ comes the infinitive.

tr: Dört sözcüğün işi. Neden kâğıt, neden ayrıntı?
en: What four words do. Why on paper, why with a detail?

tr: Partide ilk konuşma. Kim kimi nereden tanıyor?
en: The first talk at a party. Who knows whom, and from where?

tr: Burada edat yok: „sorry“ doğrudan cümle alıyor.
en: No preposition here: „sorry“ takes a clause directly.

tr: Bahçede bir düğün. Kim ne yapıyor, kim ne diyor?
en: A wedding in a garden. Who does what, and who says what?

tr: Dört cevap sırayla; en sonda evin kuralı geliyor.
en: Four answers in order; the house rule comes last.

tr: On yıllık bir arkadaşlık. Ne zaman yakın oldular?
en: A friendship of ten years. When did they become close?

tr: Bir aile geleneği. Ne zaman, kaç kişi, hangi kural?
en: A family tradition. When, how many people, and what rule?

tr: Olumsuz nereye takılıyor? İngilizce onu öne çekiyor.
en: Where does the negative go? English pulls it to the front.

tr: Önce tebrik, sonra dilek, sonra kaygı, en son gurur.
en: First the congratulation, then the wish, then the worry, and pride last.

tr: İki haber, iki dilek. Hangi kalıp hangi edatı alıyor?
en: Two pieces of news, two wishes. Which formula takes which preposition?

tr: On üç yaşında bir hesap sorusu. Dört cevap, tek karar.
en: An account at thirteen: the question. Four answers, one decision.

tr: „I don't think phones are hard. I think the menus are.“
en: „I don't think phones are hard. I think the menus are.“

tr: „We work together. Four years now.“ — okul Can'ın yolu.
en: „We work together. Four years now.“ — school is Can's way.

tr: „for“ sonrası isim geliyor; fiil gelseydi „-ing“ olurdu.
en: After „for“ comes a noun; if a verb came, it would be „-ing“.

tr: „I'm sorry I'm late. The bus stopped for twenty minutes.“
en: „I'm sorry I'm late. The bus stopped for twenty minutes.“

tr: Üç sık soru, üç kısa cevap. Hangisi hangi sorunu çözüyor?
en: Three common questions, three short answers. Which one solves which problem?

tr: „news“ tekil sayılıyor: „the news is“, „the news are“ değil.
en: „news“ counts as singular: „the news is“, not „the news are“.

tr: „Three episodes. I don't think it is as good as people say.“
en: „Three episodes. I don't think it is as good as people say.“

tr: Dört kutlama kalıbı, dört ayrı edat. Hiçbiri tahmin edilemez.
en: Four ways to congratulate, four different prepositions. None of them can be guessed.

tr: Özür ve deneyim cümleleri. „about“ iki kalıbı birden taşıyor.
en: Sentences about apology and experience. „about“ carries two formulas at once.

tr: „Thank you! On the first of October. I still can't believe it.“
en: „Thank you! On the first of October. I still can't believe it.“

tr: Aynı edat, iki ayrı devam. İsim de olur, „-ing“ de — mastar olmaz.
en: The same preposition, two ways on. A noun works, „-ing“ works — an infinitive does not.

tr: „I asked. Izmir until Sunday.“ — sınav cuma, Mert pazara kadar yok.
en: „I asked. Izmir until Sunday.“ — the exam is on Friday, Mert is away until Sunday.

tr: Aynı fiil, iki ayrı iş: „got married“ o an, „have been married“ bugün.
en: The same verb, two jobs: „got married“ is the moment, „have been married“ is today.

tr: „We celebrate the end of the summer in September.“ — 1980 başladığı yıl.
en: „We celebrate the end of the summer in September.“ — 1980 is the year it started.

tr: „I don't think it is as good as people say.“ — olumsuz „think“e takılıyor.
en: „I don't think it is as good as people say.“ — the negative hangs on „think“.

tr: „But I worry about the last chapter. It's about things I never understood.“
en: „But I worry about the last chapter. It's about things I never understood.“

tr: Telefon ve hesap cümleleri. Ayrılabilen fiiller burada nesneyi araya alıyor.
en: Sentences about a phone and an account. Separable verbs take the object in the middle here.

tr: Önce fotoğraf, sonra kuzenin evliliği, sonra Mert'in ailesi, en son Mert'in haberi.
en: First the photo, then the cousin's marriage, then Mert's family, and Mert's own news last.

tr: „Three. You forgot the meeting on Tuesday.“ — Can iki diyor, Sena üçüncüsünü hatırlatıyor.
en: „Three. You forgot the meeting on Tuesday.“ — Can says two, Sena recalls the third.
